item.text: I’ve got the core official record and a small set of independent German-language analyses. I’m now compressing that into a retained source list plus a chapter-by-chapter source plan, with explicit notes on attribution and limits.

I used the local prior as the baseline and did not re-fetch the structured country-year indicators already supplied there. I also did not score.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
Olaf Scholz was the ninth Federal Chancellor, elected on 8 December 2021, and in 2022 he led the first federal traffic-light coalition of SPD, Greens, and FDP. His office had real steering power under Article 65 of the Basic Law, but he was still constrained by Bundestag majority math, coalition bargaining, ministerial autonomy, and the fact that removal requires a constructive vote of no confidence.

**Retained Sources**
- [Olaf Scholz (2021–2025)](https://www.bundeskanzler.de/bk-en/chancellery/federal-chancellors-since-1949/olaf-scholz) | Federal Chancellery | Date: undated live biography page, current as of 2026-07-20. Fact: confirms Scholz as Federal Chancellor and leader of the first traffic-light coalition. Period fit: establishes incumbency for 2022. Ruler attribution: official self-description. Limits: retrospective and self-presenting. Contrary points: none on legal competence.
- [Wahl des Bundeskanzlers/der Bundeskanzlerin](https://www.bundestag.de/parlament/aufgaben/kanzlerwahl/kanzlerwahl-212648) | Deutscher Bundestag | Date: current page, stand 18.07.2026. Fact: the Bundestag elects the chancellor on the President’s proposal; the chancellor proposes ministers after election; removal is only via constructive no-confidence. Period fit: unchanged 2022 institutional rule set. Ruler attribution: primary constitutional procedure. Limits: institutional explanation, not event evidence. Contrary points: coalition arithmetic, not personal control, determines survivability.
- [Art. 65 GG - Einzelnorm](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gg/art_65.html) | Gesetze im Internet / Federal Ministry of Justice | Date: current consolidated legal text. Fact: the chancellor sets policy guidelines and bears responsibility; ministers run their portfolios independently within those guidelines. Period fit: directly applicable in 2022. Ruler attribution: primary law. Limits: no practical detail on coalition bargaining. Contrary points: ministerial autonomy and coalition partners blunt unilateral control.
- [Koalitionsvertrag 2021–2025](https://www.spd.de/koalitionsvertrag2021) | SPD.de | Date: 24.11.2021 metadata / late-November 2021 publication. Fact: the coalition framed its mandate around modernization, climate action, social justice, and digitization. Period fit: the binding political baseline for Scholz’s 2022 agenda. Ruler attribution: coalition-authored, therefore favorable. Limits: aspirational, not implementation evidence. Contrary points: 2022 crisis politics pushed the coalition into priorities not foregrounded here.
- [Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2008606) | Bundesregierung | Date: 27.02.2022. Fact: Scholz framed the Russian invasion as a historic turning point, announced weapons support, sanctions, and the 100-billion-euro Bundeswehr special fund. Period fit: the central 2022 pivot point. Ruler attribution: direct first-person policy statement. Limits: rhetoric plus commitment, not proof of follow-through. Contrary points: later criticism focused on delay and under-delivery.
- [Bundestag: Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz: Wir erleben eine Zeitenwende](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw08-sondersitzung-882198?enodia=eyJleHAiOjE3MDY5MzAwMDEsImNvbnRlbnQiOnRydWUsImF1ZCI6ImF1dGgiLCJIb3N0Ijoid3d3LmJ1bmRlc3RhZy5kZSIsIlNvdXJjZUlQIjoiNjYuMjQ5LjY2LjM5IiwiQ29uZmlnSUQiOiI4ZGFkY2UxMjVmZDJjMzkzMmI5NDNiNTJlOWQyY2Q2NTA1NzU0ZTE2MjIxMmEyY2UxYmI1YWYxNWMwZDRiYmZlIn0%3D.iM1SH74OhH6llgVB40VrHY_ESH8kIMzYKqy9KaO3RmY%3D) | Deutscher Bundestag | Date: 27.02.2022. Fact: corroborates the special session, broad parliamentary backing for the Ukraine response, and the legislative context around the Zeitenwende. Period fit: exact contemporaneous parliamentary record. Ruler attribution: primary parliamentary confirmation. Limits: summary page rather than full transcript. Contrary points: some parties rejected parts of the response package.
- [Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2137018) | Bundesregierung | Date: 29.09.2022. Fact: Scholz announced the 200-billion-euro economic shield and gas-price brake to cap the energy shock. Period fit: key domestic response to the 2022 energy crisis. Ruler attribution: direct government announcement. Limits: plan announcement, not impact evaluation. Contrary points: critics argued it was expensive, late, and unevenly targeted.
- [FAQ: Das beinhaltet der "Abwehrschirm" der Bundesregierung](https://www.tagesschau.de/wirtschaft/verbraucher/energiekosten-massnahmen-101.html) | tagesschau.de | Date: 29.09.2022. Fact: explains the gas and electricity price brake package, the removal of the gas levy, and the domestic policy tradeoffs. Period fit: contemporaneous independent explanation of the same policy. Ruler attribution: independent German-language public-service journalism. Limits: explanatory journalism, not primary decision record. Contrary points: highlights fiscal tension and implementation complexity.
- [Außenpolitik unter Scholz - Als Krisenkanzler in der Zeitenwende](https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/zeitenwende-deutsche-aussenpolitik-100.html) | Deutschlandfunk | Date: 26.09.2022. Fact: assesses Scholz’s post-invasion foreign policy and records sustained skepticism from the Baltics, Poland, and the US. Period fit: good for 2022 attribution and external perception. Ruler attribution: independent local-language analysis. Limits: interpretive narrative, not primary evidence. Contrary points: emphasizes that Scholz remained too cautious for many critics.
- [Bundeswehr: "Die Mittel fließen nicht" / Das mit der Zeitenwende dauert noch](https://www.zeit.de/politik/deutschland/2022-11/bundeswehr-ruestungsindustrie-olaf-scholz-bundesregierung) | DIE ZEIT | Date: 30.11.2022. Fact: by late 2022, the promised defense uplift was still not translating into fast procurement or visible readiness gains. Period fit: captures the implementation gap inside the year. Ruler attribution: independent critical journalism. Limits: editorialized analysis. Contrary points: some delays stem from procurement bureaucracy and industrial lead times, not only political hesitation.
- [Erklärungen des Auswärtigen Amts in der Regierungspressekonferenz vom 28.02.2022](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/de/newsroom/regierungspressekonferenz-2514348) | Auswärtiges Amt | Date: 28.02.2022. Fact: the government stated that Germany does not possess its own nuclear weapons and that the Bundeswehr’s role sits within NATO nuclear sharing. Period fit: exact 2022 security context and useful for 1B. Ruler attribution: primary official transcript. Limits: Q&A format, so it is narrower than a strategy paper. Contrary points: operational detail is intentionally limited.

**Compact Event Map**
- 8 Dec 2021: Scholz takes office with a three-party coalition and a reform-heavy coalition agreement.
- 24-27 Feb 2022: Russia invades Ukraine; Scholz answers with the Zeitenwende speech, sanctions, arms support, and the 100-billion-euro Bundeswehr fund.
- Spring 2022: Parliament turns the initial announcement into law and the Ukraine policy becomes more concrete.
- Summer 2022: the energy shock, inflation pressure, and coalition tradeoffs dominate domestic politics.
- 29 Sep 2022: the government unveils the 200-billion-euro economic shield and gas-price brake.
- Nov 2022: criticism sharpens over slow defense procurement and whether the Zeitenwende is moving fast enough.

**Chapter Source Plan**

- 3B: use the 27 Feb speech, Deutschlandfunk’s foreign-policy analysis, and ZEIT’s skepticism about implementation and public support.
- 4B: use the Bundestag and Basic Law pages plus the coalition agreement for office, coalition, and institutional constraints.

- 6B: use the economic-shield sources and government energy-relief announcements; if you need more detail, add health/education/welfare statistics.
- 7B: use the Bundestag institutional pages, the coalition agreement, and independent oversight-oriented coverage; if a specific corruption claim is needed, add audit or transparency sources.
